description_short.value: Mobile network operator providing voice, data and mobile money services across Ghana.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Scancom PLC 2024 Annual Report and FY2025 results

description_full.value: Scancom PLC, which trades as MTN Ghana, runs a nationwide mobile network. Most of its revenue comes from voice calls, mobile data, SMS, interconnect and roaming, with smaller amounts from handset and accessory sales. Its subsidiary MobileMoney Ltd operates the MoMo platform, which lets customers send money, pay bills and make payments from a mobile wallet. The company had about 31.2 million mobile subscribers at the end of 2025. It was incorporated in 1994, became a public company in 2016 and listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange in September 2018. Its ultimate parent is MTN Group Limited of South Africa.

description_short.value: State-controlled Ghanaian universal bank offering corporate and retail banking, with an emphasis on agriculture.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Agricultural Development Bank PLC 2024 Annual Report (report of the directors, nature of business, p. 11)

description_full.value: Agricultural Development Bank PLC (ADB) holds a universal banking licence in Ghana. Its principal activities are corporate and retail banking, and it aims to serve local and international clients with an emphasis on agriculture. It had 89 branches and agencies at the end of 2024. The bank has been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since December 2016. The Government of Ghana holds about 84% of its shares and Financial Investment Trust about 13%. After losses in 2022 and 2023 left its equity negative, ADB was recapitalised through a GHS 1.5 billion rights issue in 2024 and a further GHS 850 million deposit for shares in 2025, and returned to profit.

description_short.value: Gold miner operating the Bibiani and Chirano gold mines in Ghana, incorporated in British Columbia, Canada.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Asante Gold Corporation Annual Information Form for the period ended December 31, 2025

description_full.value: Asante Gold Corporation operates two gold mines in Ghana, Bibiani and Chirano, through 90%-owned subsidiaries. It also explores for further resources, including the Kubi Gold Project and other concessions on the Bibiani and Ashanti gold belts. The company was incorporated in British Columbia in 2011 and has its head office in Vancouver. Its shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange (ASE), the Ghana Stock Exchange (ASG), where they were listed by introduction in June 2022, the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and the OTCQX. It reports in US dollars, and in 2025 it changed its financial year end from January 31 to December 31.

description_short.value: Ghanaian universal bank serving corporate, SME and personal customers, with an asset management arm.
description_short.source: Written by us from the CalBank PLC 2025 Annual Report (reporting entity note, p. 70; our company, p. 42)

description_full.value: CalBank PLC holds a universal banking licence in Ghana. It provides corporate banking, including project, structured and trade finance, as well as commercial banking for small and medium-sized businesses and personal banking for individuals. At the end of 2025 it had 38 branches in nine regions and about 2,500 agents. Its subsidiary CalAsset Management Company Limited manages assets for third parties, and the group also has a nominee company and a pension trustee. The bank began operating in 1990 and has been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since November 2004. Losses in 2022 and 2023 left its equity negative at the end of 2023. In 2025 it raised GHS 900 million by issuing about 3.1 billion new shares through a rights issue and private placement, which brought its capital adequacy ratio back to 19.8%. SSNIT is its largest shareholder, with about 35% of the shares.

description_short.value: Oil palm grower and processor producing crude palm oil and palm kernel oil in Ghana; a subsidiary of Wilmar.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Benso Oil Palm Plantation PLC 2025 Annual Report (report of the directors, principal activities and parent company, p. 14)

description_full.value: Benso Oil Palm Plantation PLC (BOPP) grows oil palm and processes the fruit at its own mill into crude palm oil and palm kernel oil. Its plantation at Adum Banso Estate had a mature area of 4,484 hectares at the end of 2025. It also buys fruit from smallholder and outgrower farmers, and has funded the development of about 3,030 hectares of smallholder and outgrower plantings around the estate. The company has been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since April 2004. Wilmar Africa Limited owns 76.6% of its shares, and its ultimate parent is Wilmar International Limited, which is listed in Singapore.
